html:
Compact guidance

Settings → Guidance → Compact guidance uses authored shorter equivalents of built-in model instructions. The master switch defaults off. Every independently supplied block has a switch, grouped by System, Task and runtime, Skills and tools, Recovery, and Helpers, then by its owning module. Settings search matches labels, identifiers, modules and groups. Individual switches default on, remain disabled while the master is off, and retain saved choices.

Compact settings choose the full or compact variant. The Prompt Editor can customize either variant independently. Without editor overrides, an off toggle preserves the original full guidance byte-for-byte. With a saved full override, turning compact guidance off selects that customized full wording; it does not restore the shipped default.

Master Block Model receives
Off Either Full variant: valid override if present, otherwise exact shipped wording
On Off That block's full variant, with the same override rule
On On Compact variant and its valid override; full variant if no compact variant exists

Selection does not ask a model to compress instructions or reconstruct full text from a compact variant. Source matching includes whitespace and punctuation. An installation or embedded client without configuration stays off. Restoring shipped wording is an editor reset operation, separate from the compact switch.

Settings and request lifetime

The existing settings registry and runtime-controls persistence own compact selection. The separate prompt API owns wording overrides:

{"version": 1, "enabled": false, "blocks": {}}

Missing block entries select compact when enabled; explicit false selects full. Booleans, version and registered identifiers are validated strictly. Invalid saved configuration falls back to off with a diagnostic. Reset uses the existing settings reset path.

The controller publishes an immutable policy. Each logical model request captures it and the current prompt-override snapshot before prompt/tool assembly and capacity checks, including subsequent decisions in running tasks. Transport retries retain that snapshot; a separate repair or helper invocation captures the latest one. This operates independently of Prompt caching. Affected fragment and provider-continuation identities include the policy and source revisions. Compact repair and compiler layouts retain explicit section recognition.

Source ownership

The guidance package owns switch validation, request snapshots and source-bound selection. The prompt catalog loads definitions from the packaged, read-only prompts.db, compiled from explicitly named authoring inputs. Each package's guidance_compact.py is a compatibility view of that catalog, not an independent store of wording. See catalog compilation and migration for the authoring and persistence workflow.

Canonical full definitions supply source bindings and saved history. Outgoing selection resolves the selected variant and any valid override before dynamic factual values are combined with instruction templates. A changed or unknown original fails source matching and remains untouched.

flowchart LR Release[Sealed prompt catalog] --> Canonical[Canonical source and bindings] Settings[Compact choices] --> Request[Pinned request snapshots] Overrides[Prompt Editor overrides] --> Request Canonical --> Select[Verify source and select variant] Request --> Select Select --> Outgoing[Disposable messages and tool descriptions] Canonical --> History[Saved canonical history]

The catalog includes system protocol sections, behavior and runtime rules, collaboration modes, memory and Task Context instructions, every built-in Skill and tool description, native control descriptions, recovery instructions and helper templates. Legacy and Task Context prompt paths are covered. Helpers include task compilation, capability selection, structured repair, event/parameter drafting and monitor planning/judgment. Retrospective summary formatting is selectable; terminal summary generation itself is local and does not invoke a model.

Reused instructions share identifiers across delivery locations. For example, sudo guidance is one block embedded in both the system protocol and Shell description; the surrounding Shell instructions have their own switches. These composites use registered offsets in an exact known source, never searches through assembled prompts, user text or tool evidence.

Skill instructions are selected before the existing placement budgets. Prompt and tool-description placement use the same selected text, with existing availability, ordering and single-copy rules. Schemas, tool names, user instructions, custom templates, evidence and dynamic values keep their existing contracts. Custom template revisions and source mismatches retain originals and record diagnostics. Terse instructions and dense provider reference contracts deliberately use the same wording in both modes; no universal reduction ratio is promised.

History and recovery

Canonical task snapshots and durable messages retain full originals. Outgoing projections are disposable. Newly saved runtime feedback and discovery responses retain source identifiers and span parameters in _guidance_history, outside the message bytes so they cannot affect original history sizing or compaction. This metadata never enters model messages. Changed, unrecognized or custom historical text remains verbatim. Tool data and exact paged evidence are not compression inputs.

Source checks fence every span before selection. Missing/mismatched variants fall back to full text and produce content-free diagnostics in the request latency context and logging. With no Prompt Editor overrides, disabled blocks return their original value before compact lookup or rendering. With overrides, exact source validation still precedes selection of the customized full variant.

Reviewing a source change

  1. Keep the full source authoritative. Review the matching compact wording for every obligation, prohibition, condition, exception, priority, identifier and recovery instruction.
  2. Update the authoring catalog's requirement checklist, revision, fingerprints and source fixture after review. Compile and verify prompts.db using the prompt compiler commands. Checklists are review evidence, never a recipe for reconstructing full guidance.
  3. Run tests/test_compact_guidance.py, tests/test_compact_guidance_parity.py, tests/test_prompt_editor.py and relevant scenario tests. Run tests/e2e/test_compact_guidance_playwright.py for settings changes.
  4. Recompute the local savings report with PYTHONPATH=.:src .venv/bin/python scripts/compact_guidance_report.py.

The compatibility suite compares complete requests and final HTTP payloads with captures taken before this feature, including pre-existing working-tree guidance changes. It tests master-off, all-blocks-off, on-to-off restoration, individual bypass, concurrent snapshots, live decisions, retries, history integrity, custom content, placement and source drift. Browser tests cover search, keyboard controls, disabled choices, persistence and desktop/mobile layout. Prose equivalence review is separate from byte compatibility and token measurements.

Initial local measurements

These are retained fixture measurements, not a fresh benchmark of this checkout. The savings/parity fixtures currently have a different catalog revision from the runtime; source review also detects drift in tools.memory.assess.description. Those mismatches reproduce at the documentation refresh's starting revision. Keep the existing captures as evidence until a separate instruction review updates their source bindings and reruns the measurement workflow. The table does not establish current request savings or a clean parity result.

The checked-in tests/fixtures/compact-guidance-savings.json reports per-block character/UTF-8 sizes and complete synthetic request estimates. Its 1,843 blocks include 101 shorter variants. Aggregate catalog text is 333,462 full versus 302,751 compact characters; the entire catalog is never sent in one request.

These counts use native.context.request_tokens, the runtime's supported cline_character_estimate. They include final transport instruction additions, messages and tool schemas. They are estimates, not provider tokenizer counts; the script performs no inference or network requests. Two additional workloads use real core tool declarations and the existing skill-placement budgets, with synthetic availability. Their larger schemas make instruction savings a smaller share of input.

Real savings depend on selected Skills, tool schemas, evidence volume and individual switches. Release remains opt-in; the off-state compatibility checks are mandatory.
